I have been farming these 24 mu in Quzhou for 30 years. I only finished primary school, but I know my land like the back of my hand. My wife and I are both in our fifties now, and our son works in Handan, so for the heavy work I hire the tractor service. I learned farming from my father and from watching the neighbors who do well. Last year I put 20 mu into wheat followed by maize, and kept 4 mu for cotton. The cotton price was okay, but picking it is back-breaking work, so I will not plant more than 4 mu this year.

For my 20 mu of wheat, I buy improved seed from the dealer in town. I will sow 32 jin per mu — last year I used 30 jin, but my neighbor Wang used 32 and his wheat looked stronger. Before sowing, I spread one full bag of compound fertilizer per mu; each bag is 100 jin, and the dealer says it is 15-15-15. I do not care much about those numbers, but I know it has nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium all together. When the wheat turns green in spring, I will spread 20 jin of urea per mu, and another 20 jin at the jointing stage. Some people say that is a lot, but two years ago I tried to save money on fertilizer and lost nearly 100 jin per mu in yield. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. I will irrigate three times: once now at green-up if the soil is dry, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. I spray herbicide once before sowing, and insecticide twice in the spring. I use rotary tillage before sowing the wheat. If the weather cooperates, I expect about 550 kg per mu.

For maize on the same 20 mu, after we harvest the wheat in early June, I plant hybrid maize directly into the wheat stubble without plowing. No-tillage saves me time and tractor money, and everybody around here does it now. I use 2.5 kg of hybrid seed per mu. At sowing, I spread 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu, and when the plants reach the big trumpet stage I追 40 jin of urea per mu. I will irrigate twice if the summer is dry — once when the tassels come out and once when the grain is filling. I spray herbicide once at sowing and insecticide twice, because the armyworm came through last year and I cannot let that happen again. I expect about 600 kg per mu.

For the 4 mu of cotton, I rotary till the plot well in spring because cotton needs loose soil. I sow 3 jin of improved cotton seed per mu. I put 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as a base, and when the plants flower I add 30 jin of urea per mu. Cotton needs water at flowering and boll stage, so I will irrigate twice. The bollworm is terrible here — I will spray five times, better safe than sorry. I expect about 260 kg of seed cotton per mu.

My son sends some money home, but I pay for all the inputs myself. Fertilizer and pesticide prices keep rising, so I calculate every yuan. Still, I would rather spend a little too much than lose yield. I watch what the bigger farmers in the village do, and I follow them. Change is risky, and what worked last year will probably work this year.
